record.original_question: For an infinite, locally finite, one-ended, vertex-transitive graph G, is G planar exactly when for every geodesic doubly-infinite path D, the graph G − V(D) has exactly two components and both are infinite?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.2 Let G be an infinite, locally-finite, 1-ended vertex-transitive graph. Then G is planar if and only if for every geodesic D, G − V (D) has exactly two components, both infinite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be an infinite, locally finite, one-ended, vertex-transitive simple graph. Equip G with the graph metric, and call a doubly-infinite path D = (..., v_{-1}, v_0, v_1, ...) a geodesic if for all integers i < j the subpath from v_i to v_j is a shortest path in G. For such a geodesic D, let G − V(D) denote the subgraph of G induced by V(G) ∖ V(D).

Prove or disprove: G is planar (i.e., can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings) if and only if, for every doubly-infinite geodesic D in G, the graph G − V(D) has exactly two connected components, both of which are infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2025) on uniformly bisecting quasi-geodesics in vertex-transitive graphs resolves a related Kourovka Notebook problem for quasi-geodesics, showing that the uniform bisection property characterizes graphs quasi-isometric to the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane. However, the authors explicitly leave open the corresponding statement for geodesics only, which matches the conjecture in question. No proof or disproof of the geodesic-only planarity characterization for one-ended locally-finite vertex-transitive graphs has been found.

status_evidence.title: Vertex-transitive graphs with uniformly bisecting quasi-geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the quasi-geodesic version; explicitly raises as open whether the geodesic-only bisection property suffices.
status_evidence.claim: The geodesic-only version (matching the stated conjecture) is acknowledged as open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesics in Transitive Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: If a 1-ended transitive graph has every geodesic bisecting it, then the geodetic subgraph is planar (Theorem 6.1).
status_evidence.claim: Partial result toward one direction is known, but the full equivalence remains a conjecture.
